nodes.label: CQRS
nodes.rationale: Used here because the query spans four services and there is no join to write. Not worth it when read and write models are the same shape, which is most CRUD.

nodes.label: Read model (PortfolioScorecard)
nodes.rationale: Owns no truth — every column is a copy that can be deleted and rebuilt; written only by projections and read only by queries; eventually consistent, and the lag is shown deliberately. It keeps working when every other service is offline, which fan-out-per-request does not.

nodes.label: Carry resulting state, not just the delta
nodes.rationale: BenefitRealised carries RealisedToDate as well as ActualValue so the projection sets rather than adds; a redelivery with a fresh message id then cannot double-count. One contract decision removes a whole class of bug.

nodes.label: Derive counts, do not maintain them
nodes.rationale: Incrementing/decrementing RAG counters broke when a KPI recovered, because the projection could not tell a new reading from a moving one. Keeping a per-KPI status row and recomputing is self-healing; counters drift silently and forever.

nodes.label: Projections upsert, never insert
nodes.rationale: Events arrive out of order across five independent services — a KPI confirmation routinely lands before ProjectDraftCreated — so find-or-create makes ordering irrelevant except for fields that genuinely overwrite each other.

nodes.label: Rebuild the read model
nodes.rationale: A read model is a cache with a schema. Two honest rebuild routes: replay from an event store, or re-read current state from the owning services — this system does the latter because it has an outbox (a delivery mechanism whose rows are drained), not an event store.

nodes.label: Event sourcing (and why it is not CQRS)
nodes.rationale: CQRS separates read and write models; event sourcing stores state as a sequence of events. They pair well but each works without the other, and this system is CQRS without event sourcing.
